gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-tamil-sup: Round, parenthesis-like forms make Noto Sans Tamil Supplement read stocky and sturdy, with a middle band that fills the line. Autour One is the showier one, bold and bent-wire constant, while Noto Sans Tamil Supplement just keeps the plain sans text moving.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Futuristic and tile-like, Audiowide sets its letters apart with wide gaps. Noto Sans Kaithi follows with lowercase that fills the line like capitals, so paragraphs of text feel dense, steady and open at the e.
gen-almendra-display-fs-public-sans: Ornate and literary, Almendra Display throws a pronounced x-height across the heading, its letters never pinching shut. And Public Sans carries the text in a hefty lowercase, with broad openings that keep paragraphs trustworthy and easy going.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-tiktok-sans: Oxanium has uninterrupted monoline strokes and diagonals as heavy as its verticals. Its big lowercase meets TikTok Sans, whose x-height climbs nearly to cap height, and that shared largeness is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-vend-sans: Scattered, loud, full of air. Vend Sans brings a ruler-drawn line with curves that never thin at the turns, which is the pair's strongest quality against Paprika's reed-like counters.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-sulphur-point: Bold and wide-striding, Revalia spreads its letters apart with an open-curved g. Sulphur Point holds a marker-like line weight with bulky lowercase, and if the heading shrinks, that sans body will quickly outweigh it.
gen-nixie-one-archivo: Nostalgic pencil-thin lines in Nixie One never thicken or thin, with open curves that leave clear gaps between strokes. Archivo is the sturdier voice, its large x-height and outward curves doing the talking.
gen-nixie-one-fs-epilogue: Nixie One opens with nostalgic, retro-tech curves and a constant stroke from top to baseline. And Epilogue answers with a larger lowercase and stubby ascender tips, so the sans-serif body feels sturdier than the heading above.
gen-nixie-one-fs-fira-sans: Wide s curves and a larger-than-usual x-height give Fira Sans an unclenched, clean feel with no thick-thin shift. Nixie One is best as a delicate, retro-tech heading, while Fira Sans handles the heavy lifting as a plain sans text face.
gen-nixie-one-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans makes words look sturdy and large, its e opening clearly to the right. Nixie One does best as a thin, tube-like heading line, while Merriweather Sans does best at carrying weight in the text.
